column1: # scripts/teardown-guard-methods.tsv — the seed method list for
# Every method here writes an index's DURABLE state — redb corpus, HNSW
# snapshot, or the on-disk paths those live under. A call to one of them must
# hold the shared side of that index's teardown lock
# The first eight rows are the grep terms the hand-written table in
# `remove_chunks_from_stores` are the ninth and tenth: they delete from redb via
# `delete_chunks_from_redb` and were absent from that hand-written list, which is
# why `watch_loop::handle_modified`'s stale-chunk removal ran unguarded through
# Adding a method here WIDENS the gate: every call site of it must then be
# guarded in its own scope or declared in scripts/teardown-guard-manifest.tsv.
# Lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored.
# KNOWN LIMIT, stated plainly: this list is hand-maintained. A brand-new
# durable-write method on `CodeIndexer` is not discovered by the gate until
# someone adds it here. The gate closes the "existing method, new call site"
# drift (which is what happened three times); it does not close "new method".
